# Crypto golden vectors (C16) — format v1

Golden vectors for antseal's crypto primitives, in the Q4 envelope schema
(`../../README.md`), plus **the independent-implementation cross-check** the
spec mandates before the format freeze (MVP-SPEC.md line 5; tasks/C.md C16).

**Everything in this directory is NON-SECRET, fixed, public test fixture
material** (project rule 6). The master secret `W` is the documented fixed
test seed — the byte pattern `00 01 02 … 1f` (`testdata/README.md`,
"Secret-material convention") — and every key, salt, seed and nonce below is
a deterministic function of it. No real vault or wallet material may ever
appear here.

## The cross-check claim, stated precisely

A vector generated by the same code it validates proves nothing. Every
`expect` value in this directory was produced by an implementation
**independent of the Rust code that executes it**, so a green
`cargo test -p antseal-core vector_` run *is* cross-implementation
agreement. Per surface, the vehicle and why it is genuinely independent:

| Surface | Independent vehicle | Why it is independent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HKDF (C2) | `../hkdf/gen_vectors.py` (C3) — RFC 5869 from Python stdlib `hmac`/`hashlib` | Different language, different HMAC implementation, no shared code with `hkdf`/`sha2`. Landed at C3; C16 extends its *coverage* — the salts, keys and seeds every vector below chains through are re-derived here at **new (label, id) pairs** beyond C3's one-id-per-label file. |
| Commitments (C6) | `reference.py` — SHA-256 over `tag ‖ salt ‖ msg`, Python stdlib | Different language and hash implementation; the preimage assembly is written from MVP-SPEC.md line 79 rather than shared with `tagged_sha256`. |

`reference.py` is **not** trusted on assertion alone: it validates every
primitive it implements against that primitive's *published known-answer
vectors* before any generator uses it, and additionally against libsodium
(PyNaCl) and OpenSSL (`cryptography`) when those are installed. Run it:

```sh
python3 reference.py          # prints one line per known-answer check
```

Currently checked: RFC 5869 A.1 + A.3 (HKDF-SHA256, including the empty-salt
case antseal relies on), RFC 8439 §2.3.2 / §2.5.2 / §2.8.2 (ChaCha20 block,
Poly1305, AEAD), draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha §2.2.1 + A.3.1 (HChaCha20 and the
full XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD), RFC 8032 §7.1 (Ed25519).

## Files

- `commitments.json` — kind `commitments`: the four salted commitments
  (`unit`/`raw`/`canon`/`path`), each with its frozen domain tag, its HKDF
  salt label, the derived salt, the message, and the digest
  (MVP-SPEC.md lines 79, 93–95).
- `reference.py` — the independent reference implementations (Python
  standard library only) plus their known-answer self-test.
- `gen_vectors.py` — emits the vector files from `reference.py`. Runs the
  self-test first and refuses to emit anything if it fails.

## Regenerating (verify only — never a silent rewrite)

Committed vectors are retained forever and frozen by Q6
(`docs/dependency-policy.md` §4; `../../README.md`). A byte change to a
frozen vector is a **format event** requiring an explicit justification and
a format-version bump — never a drive-by regeneration. Run the generators
to *verify*:

```sh
cd testdata/vectors/v1/crypto
python3 gen_vectors.py commitments | diff - commitments.json
```

`gen_vectors.py` sets `sys.dont_write_bytecode` so running it never drops a
`__pycache__/` into the vector tree (which the Q4 runner would — correctly —
fail on as an unclassifiable file).

## What executes these

- `crates/antseal-core/tests/vector_runner.rs` — the generic Q4 runner;
  discovers everything here by walking the tree, no hardcoded list.
- `crates/antseal-core/tests/crypto_vectors.rs` — the C16 acceptance
  anchors: pins each file's exact path, kind, and entry count, so a
  *deleted* vector fails too (the runner alone cannot see a file that is
  no longer there).

Both carry the reserved `vector_` test-name marker, so the three
`cross-os-*` CI lanes prove byte-stability on Linux, macOS and Windows
(CONTRIBUTING.md, "Cross-OS suite naming").

## Vector-file coverage notes

**Commitments.** All four commitment kinds; the empty message and the empty
path (degenerate inputs must be well-defined); a 256-byte message; a
non-ASCII UTF-8 path; a message with genuine trailing `0x00` bytes; and a
`raw`/`canon` pair at the *same* `file_id`, which pins that the two content
commitments share one `file_salt` while `path_commit` does not
(MVP-SPEC.md line 95). Each entry carries its domain tag and salt label as
their own fields, so a tag renumbering or a salt-label swap breaks the
vector instead of being silently re-derived from it.
